analysis.title: Applied Materials Inc. (AMAT): First Take: Solid quarter, with upside to guidance
key_insights: GS expects AMAT to trade modestly higher after a solid quarter with FY1Q guidance above the Street, against elevated investor expectations.
GS says investor positioning was somewhat constructive into the print, given incrementally positive WFE commentary from peers and continued supply tightness, despite the recent sector-wide selloff.
GS reads management's constructive forward commentary as implying sustainability in coming quarters.

GS lists three focus items for the call: (1) incremental upside to CY26 WFE and early framing of CY27, supported by 8-quarter visibility; (2) DRAM/HBM upside from ongoing greenfield buildouts; (3) AGS momentum driving incremental process-control revenue.
Reported revenue was $10.41bn, versus GS $10.51bn and Street $10.33bn. Gross margin was 50.6% versus 50.5% for both GS and the Street. Non-GAAP EPS was $4.16 versus GS $4.14 and Street $4.07.

Segment mix diverged from estimates: DRAM revenue $2.64bn vs GS $2.25bn and Street $2.30bn, NAND $720mn vs GS $552mn and Street $541mn, Foundry, Logic and Other $4.64bn vs GS $5.33bn and Street $5.16bn.
AGS revenue of $1.90bn was above GS and the Street at $1.85bn.
FY1Q guidance midpoint revenue is $11.10bn (range $10.6-11.6bn) versus GS $11.02bn and Street $10.88bn. Non-GAAP EPS guidance is $4.15-$4.55 (midpoint $4.35) versus GS $4.21 and Street $4.23.
GS expects a neutral read-through for LRCX (Buy) and, to a lesser extent, KLAC (Neutral), since both have already reported and have similar end-market exposures.
GS keeps a Buy on AMAT with a 12-month price target of $670, based on 32x P/E on normalized EPS of $21.00. The stock closed at $395.08 on 11 Nov, implying 69.6% upside.

market_movers.rationale: Quarter was solid and FY1Q guidance is above the Street. The target rests on 32x P/E applied to normalized EPS of $21.00.
GS expects a neutral reaction to the AMAT print, since LRCX has already reported and has similar end-market exposures.
GS expects a neutral reaction, to a lesser extent than for LRCX, since KLAC has already reported.

sector_views.rationale: GS cites incrementally positive WFE commentary from peers, continued supply tightness, and 8-quarter visibility. This is inferred from the AMAT Buy and the constructive framing, not an explicit sector stance.

earnings_insights: AMAT FY4Q (CY3Q26) reported revenue $10.41bn, +53.1% y/y and +14.2% q/q, vs GS est $10.51bn and Street consensus $10.33bn.
AMAT reported gross margin 50.6% vs GS est 50.5% and Street consensus 50.5%. Operating margin was 35.3% vs GS est 35.3% and Street consensus 35.1%.
AMAT reported non-GAAP EPS $4.16 vs GS est $4.14 and Street consensus $4.07.
AMAT reported DRAM revenue $2,639mn vs GS est $2,251mn and Street consensus $2,296mn. NAND was $720mn vs GS est $552mn and Street consensus $541mn.
AMAT reported Foundry, Logic and Other revenue $4,638mn vs GS est $5,330mn and Street consensus $5,157mn. AGS was $1,896mn vs GS est $1,852mn and Street consensus $1,850mn.

AMAT guided FY1Q (CY4Q26E) revenue to a $11.10bn midpoint (range $10.6-11.6bn), +5.3% q/q implied by midpoint per the guidance table and +58.3% y/y at the high end. GS est $11.02bn and Street consensus $10.875bn.
AMAT guided FY1Q non-GAAP EPS to $4.15-$4.55 (midpoint $4.35) vs GS est $4.21 and Street consensus $4.23.
GS estimates for AMAT: EPS $4.14 (Oct-26E), $4.21 (Jan-27E), $4.71 (Apr-27E). FY10/26E EPS is $12.87, FY10/27E $19.76 and FY10/28E $25.01.

tension_points.bull_case: Solid quarter, FY1Q guidance above the Street on revenue and margins, and constructive commentary implying sustainable growth, with 8-quarter visibility and DRAM/HBM and AGS momentum.
tension_points.bear_case: Investor expectations were elevated going in, and the segment mix was uneven: Foundry, Logic and Other missed GS and the Street by 10-13%. Export restrictions and China-based supplier share gains are named risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Incremental export restrictions or local China-based supplier share gains, per the report's stated downside risks.
